title: Sequence-skip quant artifact profiling notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing an odd class of artifacts we've observed in the fieldbench and internal smoke tests: intermittent 'sequence-skip' events during decode when running low-precision kernels (INT8 / AWQ / GPTQ variants). The symptom is a bursty latency profile where prefill + a short decode step looks normal, then suddenly the token generation loop skips several microsteps (observed as 0.0ms gaps in profiler traces) and returns with a batch of tokens a few steps later. The surface effects: p95/p99 latency spikes, occasional duplicate or truncated tokens in output, and small but measurable quality regressions on instruction benchmarks (accuracy/intent).

Why this doc exists:
- Centralize observed traces, commands, and initial hypotheses.
- Capture microprofile outputs (nvprof / perf / CUPTI traces) aligned with kernel boundaries.
- Propose experiments to differentiate kernel-level coherence issues from runtime scheduling or KV-cache unpacking delays.

High-level hypothesis (boiled down):
1) Certain quantized kernels (packed-int8 / AWQ kernels) perform buffer remapping during decode which interacts poorly with our pre-allocated KV cache stride assumptions, causing short stall-and-bulk-return behavior.
2) The stall window correlates with cross-lane barrier operations inside fused matmul+transpose kernels — latency appears when sequence length crosses certain word-alignment thresholds (e.g., multiples of 64/128).
3) Contention on PCIe/NVLink transfer queues is exacerbated by mixed-workload scheduling (prefill + background maintenance tasks) which amplifies the manifestation in bursty traffic.

Repro steps (deterministic-ish locally):
- Model: Llama2-13B (HF: llama-2-13b-chat) converted with our internal GPTQ/AWQ export. Also reproduced on a trimmed Llama-2-7b replica for faster iteration.
- Hardware: single A100-40GB and H100-80GB (dev rigs). Note H100 shows the artifact less frequently but still appears under high batch concurrency.
- Serving binary: runtime/tf-serving-kernels:main@PR-982 (see linked PR).
- Command (profiling):
  1) warm start: ./run_bench --model-path /mnt/models/llama2-13b-gptq --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --mode prefill-only --device 0
  2) full: Nsight timeline capture: NVTX markers around prefill/decode loop (10s window): NSIGHT_CMD --collect "cudaMemcpy,KernelLaunch" --output trace.nvtx 
  3) lightweight: python client/smoke_client.py --host localhost:8080 --prompt-file tests/prompt_set_small.json --stream false --trace cups
- Perf counters to capture: L2 cache misses, DRAM BW, SM active cycles, Warp-stalls, PCIe queue depth (where available).

Observed artifacts (representative traces):
- Timeline: prefill kernels (prefill_matmul) take ~12ms, first decode token ~1.8ms. Then at token ~42 the decode kernel dispatch exhibits a 7–15ms gap with no visible kernel activity on the SMs followed by a 40ms fused kernel.
- CUPTI: small spikes in cudaMemcpyAsync queue depth exactly preceding the gap.
- Nsight: blocking synchronization call from kernel->memcpy on a buffer named kv_cache_packed_remap (internal symbol).
- Perf sample: slight bump in L2 miss ratio during the gap window (not enough on its own to explain stall length).
- Quality: on 200 eval prompts (instruction-style) GPTQ variant shows 0.9% drop in exact-match metric vs FP16 baseline; tokens malformed in 3% of runs when the sequence-skip artifact triggers.

Short microbench results (representative):
- Setup: A100, model L2-13b copied to device, batch 1
- FP16 baseline: mean per-token decode time = 1.85ms, p95 = 2.4ms
- GPTQ (std kernel): mean = 1.95ms, p95 = 3.0ms, sequence-skip incidence ~0.5% of tokens
- AWQ (packed kernel): mean = 2.10ms, p95 = 8.1ms, sequence-skip incidence ~3.8%
- INT8 custom kernel (striped): mean = 2.00ms, p95 = 4.2ms, sequence-skip incidence ~1.2%

Notes on kernel behavior observed in code (reverse engineering traces):
- Packed AWQ kernels emit a remap stage for KV cache to reduce memory footprint. Remap is triggered when token index (relative to prefill base) crosses remap_stride boundary (configurable at compile-time, often 64).
- The remap path issues an asynchronous memcpy from a temporary packed buffer back into the main KV cache and then performs an inplace unpack on SMs before the next decode step.
- If the memcpy is queued on the same stream as decode, but is accompanied by an internal semaphore (fence) used by the kernel, this can block the warp scheduler until the unpack kernel completes.

Why FP16 avoids it:
- FP16 path uses a simpler KV append strategy (no remap/unpack) and so avoids the extra memcpy->unpack boundary. The prefill-to-decode latency is thus steady and doesn't have the same fence pattern.

Initial controlled experiment matrix (to run):
- Vary remap_stride compile flag: [32, 64, 128, 256] and measure sequence-skip incidence. Hypothesis: smaller stride reduces the remap bandwidth and makes more frequent smaller stalls, larger stride reduces frequency but increases latency when it occurs.
- Isolate memcpy onto a separate copy stream (cudaMemcpyAsync + streams) and use event-based synchronization instead of a kernel-semaphore. Measure p95 and incidence.
- Run with PCIe throttling / NVLink disabled to see if host<->device transfer contention matters.
- Run multi-batch concurrency (B=1,2,4) to see amplification under higher throughput.
- Compare H100 vs A100 to confirm architecture sensitivity.

Preliminary experiment results (quick runs):
- remap_stride=32: incidence up (5.6%), p95 increases modestly (median stable, p95 higher due to many small stalls).
- remap_stride=256: incidence down (0.4%), but worst-case stall when triggered ~65ms (huge).
- separate-copy-stream: incidence drops dramatically (<0.2%) and p95 reduced back close to GPTQ baseline. CPU-side overhead increased ~0.5ms due to event polling.
- H100: incidence ~half of A100 in same config; unpack kernel is faster there (vectorized transposes supported).

Implications for routing / runtime policies:
- For hosted/high-traffic customers where p95/p99 matter more than tail throughput, prefer GPTQ or FP16 kernels for steady latency SLOs.
- For Dedicated/private where cost matters, allow AWQ/packed kernels but set the remap_stride conservative default (128) and enable separate-copy-stream by default to avoid blocking decode stream.
- Provide an opt-in kernel-flags rollout feature in the console: allow customers to enable packed remap-only for low-cost mode with warnings about possible p95 spikes.

Actionable next steps (short term):
- PR: implement separate-copy-stream option in kernel-runner (Marco). Link: PR-982.
- Experiment: run remap_stride sweep at scale with traffic-replay harness (Priya). Collate incidence vs latency curves.
- Instrumentation: add NVTX markers around remap stages and expose a small console histogram of remap-trigger frequency per-model (Evan).
- Customer impact check: query error-monitoring for duplicates/truncations correlated with AWQ deployments (Aisha).

Longer-term ideas:
- Kernel redesign: upstream change to avoid unpack-on-device by performing in-place decode on packed representation (non-trivial, requires upstream algorithmic review).
- Dynamic remap tuning: choose remap_stride at runtime based on live sequence distribution observed by the route (auto-tune per-route).
- Canary policy: when rolling new quant kernels, shadow traffic through both packed and unpacked flows and compare remap incidence before promoting.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact root cause of the host-side fence — is it our runtime wrapper or a kernel-level semaphore inserted by the AWQ codegen? Need to inspect kernel source generation path.
- Why does H100 reduce incidence so much? Likely faster unpack but need micro-ops comparison.
- Are there workloads where remap actually improves end-to-end latency (e.g., very long context where memory pressure otherwise causes paging)?

Raw diagnostic snippets (for reproducibility):
- NVTX marker example: NVTX_PUSH("prefill_start"); call_kernel(prefill); NVTX_POP(); NVTX_PUSH("kv_remap_start"); cudaMemcpyAsync(..., remapStream); cudaEventRecord(e, remapStream); cudaStreamWaitEvent(mainStream, e); NVTX_POP();
- CUPTI capture command (internal tooling): capture_cupti --pid ${PID} --output /tmp/cupti_trace --metrics "sm__cycles_elapsed.avg, l2_subp0_write_bytes.sum" --duration 15s
- quick perf sample: sudo perf record -e rNNN -a -- ./serving_binary --bench-loop

Logged references and traces:
- /mnt/bench/traces/seqskip/a100-run-2026-06-03.trace (nvtx+nsight zipped)
- /mnt/bench/traces/seqskip/h100-diff-2026-06-07.trace
- linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982

Meeting notes (sync required)
- 2026-06-04: quick triage with runtime team — agreed to try separate-copy-stream change and remap_stride sweep. Marco to own PR; Priya to schedule weekly replay jobs.

Quick todo checklist:
- [ ] Push separate-copy-stream patch to staging (Marco)
- [ ] Run remap_stride matrix at 10k-req replay (Priya)
- [ ] Add remap NVTX markers to runtime release branch (Evan)

Notes to self (raw):
- When writing up results for product, show cost vs p95 curve and include a small example: "AWQ saves 18% token-cost but increases p95 by +3–5x on workloads with many mid-length sequences unless remap-stride is tuned."
- Keep this doc as living notes — will convert to a playbook after experiments are complete.

-- Aisha
